title: 5-Year TIPS auction (December reopening of the October new issue) — the leg a sibling ledger predicted in prose and nobody put on the calendar
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23 initial research, text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 auction records. Row reads verbatim `5-Year TIPS R T / Announcement Thursday, December 17, 2026 / Auction Tuesday, December 22, 2026 / Settlement Thursday, December 31, 2026` — the `T` is Treasury's TIPS marker and the `R` makes it a REOPENING of the 2026-10-22 new issue tracked as treasury-5y-tips-2026-10-22. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23, 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), one day before that event and inside its five-day corridor, and proposed because a sibling ledger has ALREADY WRITTEN ITS BASE RATE without anyone giving the auction a row to hang it on. treasury-5y-tips-2026-10-22 records, verbatim, the forward read for exactly this print: `Base rate for the reopening that follows in December, if wanted: TIPS reopenings print a tenor-specific constant below their own CUSIP's new issue — $2B at 5Y (15/16 since 2019; the one exception a $25M off-cycle add-on to 912828ZJ2 on 2020-07-10, i.e. 15/15 on scheduled reopenings) and 10Y, but $1B at 30Y, so the widely-quoted `$2B below` is NOT a universal TIPS rule.` With sb0590 guiding the October new issue FLAT at $26B, that rule reads $24B here — a prediction sitting in prose in another ledger with no event to score it against. The whole 5-Year TIPS complex is tracked in this calendar at exactly one row (the 10-22 new issue), so the December reopening was invisible. SECOND REASON, and it is why the FRN's sweep found it: it settles 2026-12-31, i.e. the year-end block, while the FRN one day later settles 12-28 — the two legs of the same 12-17 announcement split across the holiday, which is the operational shape the FRN ledger measures. This proposal REGISTERS NOTHING OF ITS OWN: the $24B read belongs to treasury-5y-tips-2026-10-22 and is deliberately not re-registered here, and the breakeven channel (5Y breakeven, inflation expectations at the five-year point) belongs to that ledger too. It exists to give the auction a calendar row so its own never-assessed research can score what a sibling already reasoned out. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
